capture.notes: Live BTicino F461 (firmware 2.0.11 / WHO 13 device type 200 / WHO 1013 134.15.5.0) WHO 4 capture of 2026-10-24 on the physical test plant's Living Now KW4691 standalone thermostat at Zone 2 (BT-F430/2 heating valve as actuator 1, BT-F430/4 fan coil as actuator 2, heating season, no central unit), recorded with OWNd master. Purpose: the causal before / trigger / after evidence asked for on MyHOME pull request 791 (what moves dimension 12, the setpoint in force, and dimension 14, the last commanded value): a bezel turn, 480 fast alternating dimension 12 / 14 reads, the antifreeze command *4*102*2##, the dimension 7 templates *#4*2*#7*1*3## / *#4*2*#7*2*3##, bezel presses in Manual and in antifreeze, and climate.set_temperature writes from a local Home Assistant running the integration. Sessions: two event-only listeners (18:05-19:01 and 19:02-19:12 UTC) and short probe invocations with their own command session; each run takes its event-session frames from the listener that covered it (one source, no duplicate frames) and the probe's rows are aligned to the listener clock through the frames both sessions received (capture.runs[].probe_segments[].listener_offset_s; the same bus frame reached both sessions within 60 ms). Home Assistant's own requests (its *#4*2## polls and the *#4*2*#14*...*3## writes, the *#4*2*60## humidity polls) were sent on its session and are not rows; capture.home_assistant_requests lists them from its debug log, their echoes are in the event-session frames. Timing: t is one monotonic axis over all runs (capture.runs[].t_offset is each run's start; t - t_offset is the time since that run's first frame); command-session rx rows carry t_estimated = true because the session hands the replies over as a batch with the ACK / NACK, so they are placed at their request's t; result.events_after holds only the event-session frames that arrived while the request was pending (tx.t <= t <= result.t).

runs.purpose: the listener's first frames are the bezel turn on the KW4691 at 18:07:55 UTC (dimension 12 29.0 then 18.0, the season frame and the measured temperature; no dimension 14, no dimension 13); 49 s later the probe reads dimension 14, 12 and *#4*2##: 18.0 everywhere; the second *#4*2## burst is Home Assistant's own poll

480 alternating *#4*2*12## / *#4*2*14## reads 0.6 s apart for 5 min 45 s while Home Assistant wrote *#4*2*#14*0210*3## (18:11:46 UTC) and *#4*2*#14*0235*3## (18:13:39 UTC): both dimensions follow each write within one poll cycle; then 42 min of idle listening (humidity pushes, temperature, the gateway clock)

*4*102*2## (antifreeze) splits the dimensions: 12 reports the protection setpoint 7.0 while 14 keeps 23.5; *#4*2*#14*0235*3## brings the zone back to heating with 12 = 14 = 23.5; the *#4*2## burst at 18:58:46 UTC is Home Assistant's own poll; the listener ends on the valve's dimension 20 echo

baseline: Home Assistant wrote *#4*2*#14*0210*3## at 19:02:04 UTC (the listener's first frames are its echo), the probe polls *#4*2## (12 = 14 = 21.0); the dimension 7 templates *#4*2*#7*1*3## and *#4*2*#7*2*3## (answered as heating comfort 21.0 / cooling comfort 25.0 with the mode frames *4*108*2## / *4*208*2##), the season flips *4*0*2## then *4*1*2## and the setpoint 22.5 that followed, read back on both dimensions; restore 23.5; the *#4*2## burst at 19:05:32 UTC is Home Assistant's own poll

bezel +0.5 in Manual at 19:10:42 UTC (dimension 12 24.0, the valve opens), *4*102*2## (12 = 7.0, 14 = 24.0), bezel +0.5 in antifreeze at 19:11:10 UTC (the zone returns to heating at 7.5 on dimension 12, then 14), *4*102*2## again (12 = 7.0, 14 = 7.5), Home Assistant's *#4*2*#14*0235*3## at 19:12:26 UTC realigns both; the listener kept running after the last poll (19:12:37 UTC), those frames are not included
